items.summary: The Waste Management Act says no one may improperly discard waste, and violations carry penalties. Leaving garbage on a road or in the mountains is one example. Carelessly throwing cans, cigarette butts and other litter on streets or in parks is also prohibited by the Minor Offenses Act (軽犯罪法).

items.title: One person's bad manners can shape how all foreign residents are seen
items.summary: Rules and manners for daily life differ from country to country. Most bad manners happen because people did not know things are different in Japan, or simply slipped up. Even so, easily noticed behavior such as talking loudly on trains, cutting in line or putting out garbage the wrong way is sometimes covered in the news and on social media. It can turn into views like 'foreigners are...', and all the foreign residents who follow the rules can end up being looked at harshly. This does not mean those views are right. People from any country can make similar mistakes in a place they are not used to. Knowing in advance which behavior often causes problems makes misunderstandings and friction easier to avoid. You can check them in the related items below.
do: Assume things may be different in Japan, and check first
Follow signs and notices when there are any
If someone asks you to stop, stop right away
dont: Assume things work the same as in your own country

ja.summary: 盲導犬、介助犬、聴導犬の「ほじょ犬」は、障害のある人の大切なパートナーで、ペットではありません。ほじょ犬はユーザーの指示に集中する必要があるため、話しかける、じっと見つめる、触るなど気を引く行為は避けるよう呼びかけられています。食べ物や水もあげません。気が散ると、ユーザーが安全に歩けなくなります。

items.title: Cover your mouth and nose when you cough or sneeze
items.summary: When you cough or sneeze, cover your mouth and nose with a mask, tissue or handkerchief. If there is no time, use your sleeve or the inside of your elbow. Coughing or sneezing without regard for others is also listed among behaviors people find annoying on trains.
do: Cover your mouth and nose with a mask, tissue or handkerchief
If there is no time, use your sleeve or the inside of your elbow
dont: Cough or sneeze openly toward people around you

ja.title: せきやくしゃみは口と鼻を覆う
ja.summary: せきやくしゃみをするときは、マスク、ティッシュ、ハンカチなどで口と鼻を覆います。とっさのときは、袖やひじの内側を使います。周りに配慮しないせきやくしゃみは、電車内で迷惑に感じる行為としても挙げられています。

items.label: manner

sources.title: Understanding and Mastering Japanese Manners and Etiquette | Guide | Travel Japan
生活・就労ガイドブック（多言語） | 出入国在留管理庁

items.title: Start with a light bow
items.summary: A light nod or bow when you meet someone or enter or leave a shop comes across as polite. You do not need to memorize detailed rules of bowing. Exchanging greetings with your neighbors day to day makes trouble less likely.
do: Give a light bow when you meet someone
Greet your neighbors when you see them
dont: Skip greetings because you worry about bowing correctly

ja.title: あいさつは軽いおじぎから
ja.summary: 人に会ったときや店に出入りするときは、軽くうなずいたり頭を下げたりするだけで丁寧に伝わります。おじぎの細かい決まりを覚える必要はありません。近所の人と日ごろからあいさつを交わしておくと、トラブルが起きにくくなります。

items.label: manner

sources.title: ヘルプマーク｜障害者施策｜東京都福祉局
ご存知ですか？ マタニティマーク - 埼玉県

items.title: Know what the Help Mark and the Maternity Mark mean
items.summary: The Help Mark is worn by people who need help or consideration even when it does not show, such as people with artificial limbs or joints, internal disabilities or intractable diseases, or in early pregnancy. The Maternity Mark lets people nearby know that the wearer is pregnant. When you see one, you are asked to act with consideration, such as offering your seat on trains and buses, or speaking to the person if they seem to need help.
do: Offer your seat on trains and buses
Speak to the person at a station or shop if they seem to need help
Avoid smoking near pregnant people
dont: Look with suspicion at someone in a priority seat because they look well

ja.title: ヘルプマークとマタニティマークの意味を知っておく
ja.summary: ヘルプマークは、義足や人工関節を使っている人、内部障害や難病のある人、妊娠初期の人など、外見では分からなくても助けや配慮が必要な人が身に着けるマークです。マタニティマークは、妊娠していることを周りに知らせるマークです。見かけたら、電車やバスで席を譲る、困っていそうなら声をかけるなど、思いやりのある行動が呼びかけられています。

items.label: manner

sources.title: 生活・就労ガイドブック（多言語） | 出入国在留管理庁

items.title: For minor illness or injury, go to a nearby clinic
items.summary: Medical institutions in Japan have different roles, and for minor illness or injury you first go to a nearby clinic. If you do not show your My Number health insurance card or similar proof, you pay the full medical costs yourself. If you cannot speak Japanese, you can ask your municipality, an international exchange association or an NPO for help.
do: Go to a nearby clinic for minor symptoms
Bring your My Number health insurance card or similar proof
If language worries you, ask your municipality or similar service
dont: See a doctor without your My Number health insurance card or similar proof

ja.title: 軽い病気やけがは近くの診療所へ
ja.summary: 日本の医療機関は役割が分かれていて、軽い病気やけがなら、まず身近な診療所に行きます。マイナ保険証などを提示しないと、医療費が全額自己負担になります。日本語が話せないときは、市区町村や国際交流協会、NPO に相談できます。

items.title: Mind your voice and how much space you take up in crowded places
items.summary: Talking loudly in crowded places such as streets and station passages, or blocking the way in a large group, is seen as a nuisance. Talking itself is not the problem, and a soft voice is fine.
do: Lower your voice in crowded places
Keep aisles and doorways clear
dont: Block the way by spreading out in a large group
Stop in front of doorways

ja.title: 人の多い場所では声と広がり方に気をつける
ja.summary: 道や駅の通路など人の多い場所で大声で話したり、大勢で道をふさいだりすると、迷惑な行為と受け取られます。話すこと自体がいけないわけではなく、小さな声なら問題ありません。

items.label: manner

sources.title: バリアフリー設備の適正利用について／千葉県

items.title: Do not stand on or leave things on tactile paving
items.summary: Tactile paving, the blocks with raised bumps on roads and station floors, guides people with visual impairments, who feel them through the soles of their feet as they walk. Lined blocks show the direction to walk, and dotted blocks mark places that need care, such as before stairs or crosswalks. Bicycles or signs left on or around them, or people standing on them, can cause someone to trip or collide.
do: Stop or wait for people away from tactile paving
dont: Leave bicycles, bags or signs on or around tactile paving
Stand still on tactile paving

ja.title: 点字ブロックの上で立ち止まったり物を置いたりしない
ja.summary: 道や駅の床にある、表面に突起のある点字ブロック（視覚障害者誘導用ブロック）は、目の不自由な人が足の裏で感じながら歩くための道しるべです。線状のブロックは進む方向を、点状のブロックは階段や横断歩道の前など注意が必要な場所を示します。上や周りに自転車や看板が置かれていたり、人が立ち止まっていたりすると、転倒や衝突の原因になります。

items.label: manner

items.title: Flush your toilet paper
items.summary: With Japanese flush toilets, use the paper provided and flush it after use. Some countries have a custom of putting used paper in a bin, but the provided paper rarely clogs the toilet here. Where there are dedicated toilet slippers, change into them.
do: Use the paper in the toilet and flush it
Change into toilet slippers if there are any
dont: Put used paper in the bin

ja.title: トイレットペーパーは流す
ja.summary: 日本の水洗トイレでは、備え付けの紙を使い、使った紙はトイレに流します。使った紙をごみ箱に捨てる習慣の国もありますが、備え付けの紙なら詰まることはめったにありません。トイレ専用のスリッパがある場所では履き替えます。

items.label: manner

sources.title: 2025年度 駅と電車内の迷惑行為ランキング | 日本民営鉄道協会

items.title: Hold your umbrella so it does not hit people
items.summary: On rainy days, a wet umbrella that touches people or a tip pointed at the person behind you is a nuisance and can be dangerous. Hold a closed umbrella close to your body with the tip pointing down.
do: Hold a closed umbrella close to your body with the tip down
dont: Carry an umbrella sideways
Let a wet umbrella touch people or seats

ja.title: 傘は人に当たらないように持つ
ja.summary: 雨の日に、ぬれた傘が人に当たったり、傘の先を後ろの人に向けたりすると、迷惑で危険です。たたんだ傘は先を下に向けて、体の近くで持ちます。

items.title: Notify your municipality after moving
items.summary: After you start living at a new address, submit a moving-in notification (tennyu-todoke) to the municipality within the legal deadline. Moves within the same municipality use a change-of-address notification (tenkyo-todoke). Failing to notify without good reason can lead to an administrative fine. Check the deadline on the official page.
do: Bring your residence card or special permanent resident certificate to the counter
Check the deadline on the official page and go early
dont: Keep living there without notifying

ja.summary: 新しい住所に住み始めたら、法律で決められた期限内に市区町村へ転入届を出します。同じ市区町村の中で引っ越したときは転居届です。正当な理由なく届け出をしないと、過料の対象になります。期限は公式ページで確認してください。

With a My Number Card, you can submit it online through Mynaportal

ja.summary: 別の市区町村へ引っ越すときは、前もって今の市区町村に転出届を出します。日本を出て海外で暮らす場合も、原則として届け出が必要です。

items.title: It's customary to greet neighbors after moving
items.summary: It isn't required, but people often greet their neighbors after moving in: the rooms on either side in an apartment building, or a few nearby houses. This follows a guide from Higashihiroshima City, Hiroshima.
do: Keep it short and simply introduce yourself

ja.title: 引っ越したら近所にあいさつする習慣がある
ja.summary: 義務ではありませんが、引っ越したときに近所へあいさつに行く習慣があります。集合住宅なら両隣、一戸建てなら周りの数軒が目安です。これは広島県東広島市の案内の例です。

items.title: Leave nothing behind when you move out
items.summary: When you leave a room, leave neither belongings nor garbage. This is a promise on the checklist in the housing guidebook from the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism.
do: Clear out all belongings and garbage before leaving
dont: Leave unwanted items or garbage in the room

ja.title: 退去するときは部屋に何も残さない
ja.summary: 部屋を出るときは、物もごみも残しません。国土交通省の部屋探しガイドブックのチェックシートにある約束です。

items.title: Arrange electricity, gas and water yourself
items.summary: Before moving, tell the electricity company, the gas company and the municipal water office that you are moving. To start gas at your new home, you must be present when it is turned on.
do: Contact each of them early once your move is set
Contact the gas company and be present when the gas is turned on
dont: Move out without telling them

ja.title: 電気・ガス・水道の手続きは自分でする
ja.summary: 引っ越しの前に、電力会社、ガス会社、市区町村の水道担当へ移転の連絡をします。新しい家でガスを使い始めるときは、開栓に本人の立ち会いが必要です。

items.title: Don't ride in unlicensed taxis (shirotaku) or carry paying passengers yourself
items.summary: Carrying passengers for money in a private car without government permission is called "shirotaku" (白タク) and is prohibited under the Road Transport Act. You may be approached at airports or tourist spots, or such rides may be arranged through ride apps. In an unlicensed taxi, you may not receive proper compensation if there is an accident. Use licensed taxis or authorized services.
do: Use licensed taxis at a taxi stand
With ride apps, check that the ride is a licensed taxi or an authorized service
dont: Get into a private car whose driver approached you at an airport or station
Carry people in your own car for money

ja.title: 許可のない車（白タク）に乗らない・自分で客を運ばない
ja.summary: 国の許可なく、自家用車でお金をもらって客を運ぶことは「白タク」と呼ばれ、道路運送法で禁止されています。空港や観光地で声をかけられたり、配車アプリで手配されたりすることがあります。白タクでは、事故にあっても十分な補償を受けられないおそれがあります。正規のタクシーや、許可を受けたサービスを使います。

items.title: Stand still on escalators
items.summary: Some municipalities have ordinances requiring people to stand still on escalators, on either side. The link is one prefecture's example. Follow the notices at stations and facilities.
do: Stand still on the steps
Follow the notices at stations and facilities
dont: Walk or run on the escalator

ja.title: エスカレーターでは立ち止まって乗る
ja.summary: エスカレーターでは、左右どちらの側でも立ち止まって利用するよう、条例で定めている自治体があります。リンク先は一つの県の例です。駅や施設の案内に従います。

do: Check the hours and boarding position on platform and car signs
If unsure, ask station staff

ja.title: 女性専用車の表示を確認する

Use the overhead rack if you can

items.title: How you pay on a bus depends on the route
items.summary: On buses where the fare depends on distance, take a numbered ticket when you board, then check the number on the board and pay when you get off. On buses with a flat fare, you pay when you board. Some buses do not accept IC cards, and some machines do not give change.
do: Take a numbered ticket when you board, if there is one
Check whether IC cards work and have coins ready
dont: Board without taking the ticket

ja.title: バスの運賃の払い方は路線で違う
ja.summary: 距離で運賃が変わるバスでは、乗るときに番号の書かれた整理券を受け取り、降りるときにボードで番号を確かめて運賃を払います。どこまで乗っても同じ運賃のバスでは、乗るときに払います。IC カードが使えないバスや、おつりが出ない機械もあります。

items.title: On buses, wait until the bus stops before you stand up
items.summary: On local buses, passengers fall and get hurt when the bus shakes as it starts, stops or brakes suddenly. Many of those hurt are older people. Even as your stop gets close, stay seated until the bus has come to a complete stop. When standing, hold on firmly to a handrail or strap.
do: Stand up only after the bus has come to a complete stop
Hold on firmly to a handrail or strap when standing
dont: Change seats or walk to the exit while the bus is moving

ja.title: バスでは、止まってから席を立つ
ja.summary: 路線バスでは、発車や停車、急ブレーキのときの揺れで乗客が転び、けがをする事故が起きています。けがをする人には高齢の人が多くいます。降りる停留所が近づいても、バスが完全に止まってから席を立ちます。立っているときは、手すりやつり革をしっかり持ちます。

items.summary: Listening to loud music on trains and buses disturbs others. Keep sound from leaking out of your earphones, and do not play sound through your phone's speaker.
do: Turn the volume down and make sure no sound leaks
dont: Play sound through your phone's speaker

ja.title: イヤホンの音漏れに気をつける
ja.summary: 電車やバスの中で大きな音で音楽を聞くと迷惑になります。イヤホンから音が漏れないようにし、スマートフォンの音を外に出して再生しないようにします。

dont: Eat or drink in a crowded car

ja.title: 混んだ車内では飲食を控える

ja.summary: 電車やバスの中で大きな声で話したり騒いだりすると、迷惑になります。会話をするときは、周りの迷惑にならない小さな声で話します。

Follow the onboard notices near priority seats

ja.title: 電車やバスの中では通話しない

ja.summary: 大きな災害のときは電話がつながりにくくなり、音声で伝言を残せる「171」が運用されます。普段は使えず、音声案内は日本語のみで、海外からは使えません。文字で伝言を残せる「web171」もあります。電話はなるべく控え、データ通信を使いましょう。

items.title: When the ground shakes, protect yourself first
items.summary: When you see or hear an earthquake early warning, or feel shaking, stay calm and protect yourself first. Indoors, protect your head and take cover under a sturdy desk or similar. Do not rush outside, and do not force yourself to go and put out a fire. Outdoors, watch out for falling block walls, signs and broken glass. In an elevator, stop at the nearest floor and get out. On trains and buses, hold on firmly to a strap or handrail.
do: Protect your head and take cover under a sturdy desk or similar
Outdoors, keep away from block walls, signs and glass

On trains and buses, hold on firmly to a strap or handrail

Force yourself to put out a fire while it is still shaking

ja.title: 揺れたら、まず身の安全を守る
ja.summary: 緊急地震速報を見聞きしたときや揺れを感じたときは、あわてずに、まず身の安全を守ります。家の中では頭を守り、丈夫な机の下などに隠れます。あわてて外へ飛び出したり、無理に火を消しに行ったりしません。外では、ブロック塀や看板、割れたガラスの落下に気をつけます。エレベーターでは最寄りの階で止めて降り、電車やバスではつり革や手すりをしっかり持ちます。

items.title: Watch out for heatstroke on hot days
items.summary: Heatstroke can happen indoors and at night, and it can be life-threatening. When a heatstroke alert is issued, drink water and take salt before you feel thirsty, use your air conditioner properly, and avoid going out unless necessary. People around older people and others at risk should check on them.

Use the air conditioner instead of putting up with the heat
Check the heatstroke alerts

ja.title: 暑い日は熱中症に気をつける
ja.summary: 熱中症は室内でも夜でも起こり、命に関わることがあります。熱中症警戒アラートが出たら、のどが渇く前に水分と塩分をとり、エアコンを適切に使い、不要不急の外出を避けます。高齢の人などには、周りから声をかけます。

items.title: Drive on the left, and always stop at red lights and stop signs
items.summary: In Japan, vehicles drive on the left side of the road. Stop at red lights, and where there is a stop sign (止まれ), come to a full stop before the stop line and check left and right. When someone is crossing or about to cross at a crosswalk, stop before it and let them go first. Traffic rules and signs in Japan can differ from those in other countries.

Come to a full stop at stop signs and check left and right
Give way to pedestrians at crosswalks

Drive through a crosswalk without stopping when someone is about to cross

ja.title: 車は左側通行。赤信号と「止まれ」で必ず止まる
ja.summary: 日本では、車は道路の中央から左の部分を通行します。赤信号では止まり、「止まれ」の標識がある場所では停止線の手前で一時停止して、左右の安全を確かめます。横断歩道を渡っている人や渡ろうとしている人がいるときは、手前で一時停止して道を譲ります。日本の交通ルールや標識は、ほかの国と違うことがあります。

Enjoy flowers and scenery through photos

ja.summary: 国立公園や国定公園の特別地域などでは、自然公園法で、指定された植物を採ることや、石や土を採ることなどが規制されています。どこが規制されているかは見た目では分からないので、花や枝、石を持ち帰らず、決められた道を歩きます。

items.title: Don't take shellfish, sea cucumbers and other sea life without permission (poaching)
items.summary: Taking abalone or sea cucumbers without a license or similar authorization is punished, whether or not you are a fisher and regardless of how much you took or where. Taking turban shells, spiny lobsters and other species covered by fishing rights without authorization is also poaching. This is the same even for things you find on the beach or rocky shore. Fishing and clam digging also have rules set by law and by each prefecture, covering the gear you may use, closed areas and seasons, size limits and more. Recreational fishing by people without Japanese nationality is allowed only within a limited range, so check with the prefecture or the fishing boat operator beforehand.

dont: Take abalone or sea cucumbers

ja.title: 海の貝やナマコなどを勝手に採らない（密漁）
ja.summary: アワビとナマコは、許可などなしに採ると、漁業者かどうか、採った量や場所にかかわらず処罰されます。サザエやイセエビなど漁業権の対象になっている生き物を、権限なく採ることも密漁です。浜辺や磯で見つけたものでも同じです。釣りや潮干狩りにも法律や都道府県のルールがあり、使える道具や禁止の区域・時期、大きさの制限などが決められています。日本の国籍がない人の釣りなどは認められる範囲が限られているため、事前に都道府県や釣り船の業者に確かめます。

items.title: Don't enter off-limits places, other people's fields or private roads
items.summary: Entering a place where entry is prohibited, or someone else's fields, without a legitimate reason is prohibited under the Minor Offenses Act. Entering someone's home without permission can also be the crime of trespassing under the Penal Code. Some roads that anyone can walk on are private roads owned by individuals or others rather than the national or local government. Follow any signs closing the road or prohibiting photography. Even for photos or a shortcut, do not go in when there is a sign.

items.title: Take tax-free purchases out of Japan after customs confirmation at departure
items.summary: When you shop at a tax-free store, you pay the price including tax. When you leave Japan, you show your passport at a terminal at the airport or seaport to receive customs confirmation, and then the consumption tax is refunded. Get the confirmation before checking in your luggage. If even one item on a receipt is missing, nothing on that receipt is refunded. Consumables eaten or used in Japan are not refunded either. If you do not take items confirmed by customs out of Japan, the consumption tax is collected and you may also face penalties. Check the deadlines and refund methods on the official page or with the store.

Leave Japan carrying all the items on each receipt together

Fail to take confirmed items out of Japan

ja.title: 免税で買った物は、出国時に税関の確認を受けて国外に持ち出す
ja.summary: 免税店での買い物は、税込みの値段で払い、出国するときに空港や港の端末でパスポートを見せて税関の確認を受けると、消費税分が返金される仕組みです。確認は、荷物を預ける前に受けます。1枚の領収書の物を1つでも持っていないと、その領収書の分は返金されません。日本で食べたり使ったりした消耗品も返金されません。税関の確認を受けた物を国外に持ち出さないと、消費税を取られ、罰則の対象にもなります。期限や返金の方法は、公式ページやお店で確かめます。

Snow-covered hills are fields too, with wheat and other crops growing under the snow. Soil carried on your shoes can also harm the crops. Do not drive or walk onto gravel roads or farm roads either. Flying drones and aerial photography in the town are prohibited in principle.

Ride outside the managed area without preparation or information

ja.title: スキー場のルールを守り、管理区域の外に気軽に出ない
ja.summary: スキー場の管理区域の外は、整備されたゲレンデとはまったく違う冬山です。天気の急変や雪崩、道迷い、木への衝突など、予測しにくい危険があります。コースの表示やロープなどの目印がないため、気づかないうちに入ってしまうこともあります。救助を頼むと多額の捜索費用を請求されることがあり、天気が悪いと救助できないこともあります。スキー場のルールを守り、立入禁止の場所には入りません。

items.title: Be prepared so you don't run into bears in the mountains
items.summary: In mountains and forests, you may come across bears. Let them know people are around with a bell or your voice, don't go alone, and don't leave food, bags or rubbish behind. If you meet a bear, don't approach it. Stay calm, back away slowly while watching it, and don't turn your back and run.

Don't go alone
Take your food and rubbish with you
dont: Approach a bear
Turn your back and run

ja.title: 山ではクマに出会わないように備える
ja.summary: 山や森では、クマに出会うことがあります。鈴や声などで人がいることを知らせ、ひとりで行動せず、食べ物や荷物、ごみを置いていかないようにします。出会ったら近づかず、クマを見ながら落ち着いてゆっくり後ずさりし、背中を向けて走らないでください。

items.title: Get travel insurance, and always pay your hospital bills
items.summary: Travelers who are not covered by Japan's public health insurance may have to pay the full cost of hospital treatment themselves. Before your trip, take out travel insurance with sufficient coverage. Some travel insurance can be purchased even after arriving in Japan. If you leave medical bills unpaid, you may face stricter immigration screening the next time you come to Japan, and may even be refused entry.
do: Before your trip, take out travel insurance with sufficient coverage
Pay for the treatment you received at the hospital before you leave
dont: Travel without insurance
Go home without paying medical bills

ja.title: 旅行保険に入り、病院の費用は必ず払う
ja.summary: 日本の公的医療保険に入っていない旅行者は、病院の費用が全額自己負担になることがあります。旅行の前に、十分な補償のある旅行保険に入ります。日本に来てから入れる旅行保険もあります。医療費を払わないままにすると、次に日本に来るときの入国審査が厳しくなり、入国を断られることもあります。

items.title: Keep the noise down at night in vacation rentals
items.summary: Vacation rentals (民泊) are often in residential areas where people live. By law, hosts must explain to guests what to keep in mind to avoid noise. Follow the rules you are given, and stay quiet at night and early in the morning.

Stay quiet at night and early in the morning

ja.title: 民泊では夜の音に気をつける

items.title: Keep quiet in residential areas and don't photograph residents without asking
items.summary: Even right next to tourist spots, there are residential streets where people live. They are the setting of residents' daily lives. Talking loudly, stopping and blocking the street, or photographing residents and children without asking disturbs their lives and can make them feel uneasy. Do not enter private property without permission, even to photograph the scenery or a building. When a map app routes you through a residential street as a shortcut, pass through quietly.

Ask for permission before photographing people
Follow signs such as "Private property" or "No photography"

ja.title: 住宅街では静かにし、住む人を勝手に撮らない
ja.summary: 観光地のすぐそばにも、人が暮らす住宅街があります。そこは住む人の日常生活の場です。大きな声を出したり、立ち止まって道をふさいだり、住む人や子どもを勝手に撮ったりすると、暮らしの迷惑になり、不安を感じさせることもあります。景色や建物を撮るためでも、私有地には許可なく入りません。地図アプリの近道で住宅街を通るときも、静かに通り過ぎます。

items.title: At the sea or a river, do not swim where it is prohibited, and wear a life jacket
items.summary: At the sea, swim at beaches with lifeguards or monitors, inside the designated swimming area. Never swim where swimming is prohibited. Check the wind direction and wave height, and do not enter the water near river mouths, along breakwaters or around rocks, where strong currents flowing out to sea (rip currents) tend to form. Rivers can look calm but have uneven currents, and the water can rise suddenly when it rains upstream. Near water, wear a life jacket, keep your eyes on children, and do not play in the water when you feel unwell.
do: Swim in the designated area of a beach with lifeguards
Wear a life jacket near water
Keep your eyes on children and stay within arm's reach
dont: Swim where swimming is prohibited
Enter the water near river mouths, breakwaters or rocks
Go near a river in bad weather or when it is raining upstream

ja.title: 海や川では、遊泳禁止の場所で泳がず、ライフジャケットを着る
ja.summary: 海では、ライフセーバーや監視員がいる海水浴場で、決められた遊泳エリアの中で泳ぎます。遊泳禁止の場所では絶対に泳ぎません。風の向きや波の高さを確かめ、沖へ向かう強い流れ（離岸流）が起きやすい河口付近、堤防沿い、岩場には入りません。川は穏やかに見えても流れが一定でないことがあり、上流で雨が降ると一気に水位が上がることがあります。水辺ではライフジャケットを着て、子どもから目を離さず、体調が悪いときは遊びません。
